hooks.name: Ask for ticket if missing + validate pending terminal-typed tickets (CASE A + CASE C + priority pending-check — see post-commit for CASE B)

action.prompt:
PRIORITY CHECK — runs BEFORE everything else below (CASE A/C), on every single user message, regardless of what the message is about: check whether .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json exists. That file means a ticket ID was typed at a terminal prompt (pre-commit's manual-entry fallback, or post-commit's 'switching tickets?' y/n flow) that could NOT be validated at the git-hook level — confirmed, not assumed: JIRA_BASE_URL/JIRA_EMAIL/JIRA_API_TOKEN are unset there, so those hooks always take their 'skipped-no-credential' branch and cannot tell a real ticket from a made-up one (confirmed live: a fake ID was accepted exactly like a real one — see TODO.md). That commit/switch was deliberately deferred rather than trusted: pre-commit tracked the commit as 'none' and post-commit left the OLD ticket in current-ticket.json untouched, specifically so it can be validated for real here, via the live atlassian-rovo MCP connection, before you respond to whatever the user just asked.

If the file does NOT exist: skip this whole section and go straight to CASE A/C below, exactly as before this priority check existed.

If it DOES exist: read its typed_ticket field. Before making ANY atlassian-rovo MCP call, you MUST first call getAccessibleAtlassianResources and use the cloudId it returns for the real connected Jira instance — same requirement as CASE A/C below, for the same reason (a live run once guessed a wrong cloudId before self-correcting; do not rely on that self-correction happening again). Skip re-calling it if you already confirmed the cloudId earlier in this same conversation. Then check EXISTENCE only (not assignment — same policy as everywhere else in this hook) via getJiraIssue or searchJiraIssuesUsingJql for that exact ID.

- If it clearly does NOT exist: tell the user plainly, e.g. "<typed_ticket> (typed earlier) doesn't appear to be a real ticket — please check the ID." Delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json. Do NOT touch .kiro/current-ticket.json — leave whatever ticket_id is already there exactly as it is (pre-commit's deferral already tracked that commit as 'none'; post-commit's deferral already left the old ticket in place — neither needs undoing). Then ask which Jira ticket they're actually working on right now (mention the current one from current-ticket.json first if it's non-empty, e.g. "you're still tracked on <ticket_id> — is that right, or a different one?"), the same question CASE A2 asks — wait for their next message as its answer, handled by CASE A1/C1 below exactly like any other ticket question. Do not answer their original message yet.
- If the MCP call itself fails for any OTHER reason (network error, timeout, ambiguous response — i.e. you cannot tell whether it exists or not, as opposed to a clear not-found): do NOT block — briefly note validation couldn't be performed, then proceed exactly as if it had passed (the 'real' branch below).
- If it IS real (or validation couldn't be performed): read the current ticket_id already in .kiro/current-ticket.json. If it already equals typed_ticket exactly (e.g. the same pending check somehow runs twice), just delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json and briefly confirm it's already tracked — no need to regenerate a baseline or episode_id for a ticket that's already current. Otherwise this is a genuinely new/different ticket relative to whatever current-ticket.json says (including if it was 'none' or empty): generate a fresh baseline and episode_id by running exactly this command, same as CASE A1 (do not improvise another method — see CASE A1's comment for why): `python3 -c "import sqlite3,json,os,time,secrets; con=sqlite3.connect(os.path.expanduser('~/.config/Kiro/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb')); row=con.execute(\"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key='kiro.kiroAgent'\").fetchone(); val=row[0]; val=val.decode('utf-8') if isinstance(val,bytes) else val; usage=json.loads(val)['kiro.resourceNotifications.usageState']['usageBreakdowns'][0]['currentUsage']; print(usage); print('ep_'+format(int(time.time()),'x')+secrets.token_hex(3))"` — same two-line output as CASE A1 (line 1: credit total, line 2: new episode_id). Then write {"ticket_id": "<typed_ticket>", "credits_at_ticket_start": <line 1>, "episode_id": <line 2>} into .kiro/current-ticket.json — this fully replaces the file's contents. Delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json. Tell the user plainly it's confirmed and now being tracked (note what it replaced, if current-ticket.json had a different ticket_id before this write). THEN continue and actually answer their original message — do not stop here, this check must not silently swallow their real request.

This priority check runs on every message for as long as the pending file exists, even if the user's message looks completely unrelated — validating a flagged ticket takes priority over answering the request, per "before you respond to whatever the user just asked" above.

This hook handles two of the three cases that can start a new episode — CASE A and CASE C. (CASE B — a direct, deterministic post-commit question, the primary switch-detection mechanism — lives entirely in .githooks/post-commit, not in this AI-driven hook. CASE C below is the softer secondary safety net that can catch a switch mid-conversation, before anything has even been committed yet.)

CASE A — ticket_id is empty or missing: this is a two-step flow across two separate prompts (a hook cannot ask-then-wait-then-save within a single turn) — so branch on the current message: (A1) if the user's current message is exactly a Jira ticket ID matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ (e.g. ANG-123) or is exactly 'none', treat that message AS the answer to the pending question. If it is a real ticket ID (not 'none'), FIRST validate it actually exists in Jira before saving anything — call the atlassian-rovo MCP connection (getJiraIssue for that exact ID, or searchJiraIssuesUsingJql with a JQL like key = \"<ticket>\") to check. This is EXISTENCE-checking only, not assignment-checking — do not reject a ticket for being assigned to someone else or unassigned, only for not existing at all (see aidlc-git-conventions.md's Workflow section for why assignment-checking is explicitly out of scope). If the call clearly reports the issue does not exist: tell the user plainly, e.g. \"<ticket> doesn't appear to be a real ticket — please check the ID,\" do NOT save it, and treat this exactly like (A2) below — wait for their next message as a fresh answer attempt, don't ask again redundantly. If the MCP call itself fails for any OTHER reason (network error, MCP connection down, timeout, an ambiguous/unclear response) — i.e. you cannot tell whether it exists or not, as opposed to a clear not-found — do NOT block on this: briefly tell the user validation couldn't be performed right now, then proceed exactly as if it had passed. Once it's 'none', or a real ticket that passed validation, or validation couldn't be performed: read the current credit total AND generate a fresh episode_id by running exactly this command (do not improvise another method — the .vscdb file is binary SQLite, not line/tab-delimited text, and 'sqlite3' CLI is not installed on this machine, so both a raw `cat`/`head` read and a naive Node text-split WILL silently produce a wrong or fabricated number instead of erroring): `python3 -c "import sqlite3,json,os,time,secrets; con=sqlite3.connect(os.path.expanduser('~/.config/Kiro/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb')); row=con.execute(\"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key='kiro.kiroAgent'\").fetchone(); val=row[0]; val=val.decode('utf-8') if isinstance(val,bytes) else val; usage=json.loads(val)['kiro.resourceNotifications.usageState']['usageBreakdowns'][0]['currentUsage']; print(usage); print('ep_'+format(int(time.time()),'x')+secrets.token_hex(3))"` — this prints two lines: line 1 is the credit total, line 2 is the new episode_id. Use both verbatim, do not read either off of any other command's raw/truncated output and do not generate the episode_id yourself some other way. Then write {"ticket_id": <that value>, "credits_at_ticket_start": <line 1>, "episode_id": <line 2>} into .kiro/current-ticket.json (this fully replaces the file's contents — there is no pending_switch_to to worry about here since the file was empty), briefly confirm it's saved, then continue handling the rest of their request normally — do not ask again. (A2) Otherwise, the message is a normal work request, not an answer to a prior question — stop and ask which Jira ticket they're working on (or 'none' for work with no ticket) before doing anything else with their request, and wait for their next message to be treated as the answer per (A1).

CASE C — ticket_id is non-empty: this is the mid-session ticket-switch case (no branch change has happened, so post-checkout never cleared the file) — also a two-step flow, using a pending_switch_to field in current-ticket.json as the state signal instead of file-emptiness, since the file stays non-empty throughout this whole exchange: (C1) if current-ticket.json ALSO already has a non-empty pending_switch_to field, a switch question was asked on the previous turn — treat the CURRENT message as the answer to it, not as a new request yet. If the message is a clear affirmative (e.g. 'yes', 'switch', 'confirm', or it repeats the pending_switch_to ticket ID), the switch is confirmed: unless pending_switch_to is exactly 'none', FIRST validate it exists in Jira the same way as (A1) above (getJiraIssue or searchJiraIssuesUsingJql — existence-checking only, not assignment, same reasoning as (A1)). If it clearly does not exist: tell the user plainly it doesn't appear to be a real ticket, do NOT switch — handle this exactly like a declined switch below (remove only pending_switch_to, leave ticket_id/credits_at_ticket_start/episode_id exactly as they were), then continue with their original request normally instead of waiting for another answer. If the MCP call fails for any OTHER reason (not a clear not-found — network error, timeout, ambiguous response), do NOT block: briefly note validation couldn't be performed, then proceed with the switch anyway. Once it's 'none', or the new ticket passed validation, or validation couldn't be performed: generate a fresh baseline and episode_id for the NEW ticket by running exactly this command: `python3 -c "import sqlite3,json,os,time,secrets; con=sqlite3.connect(os.path.expanduser('~/.config/Kiro/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb')); row=con.execute(\"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key='kiro.kiroAgent'\").fetchone(); val=row[0]; val=val.decode('utf-8') if isinstance(val,bytes) else val; usage=json.loads(val)['kiro.resourceNotifications.usageState']['usageBreakdowns'][0]['currentUsage']; print(usage); print('ep_'+format(int(time.time()),'x')+secrets.token_hex(3))"` — same two-line output as in (A1). Then write {"ticket_id": <pending_switch_to's value>, "credits_at_ticket_start": <line 1>, "episode_id": <line 2>} into current-ticket.json — this REPLACES the old ticket_id, baseline, and episode_id entirely, and drops the pending_switch_to field (do not carry it over). Briefly confirm the switch happened, then continue with the rest of their request normally. If the message is NOT a clear affirmative (declines, is ambiguous, or is unrelated to the question), default to NOT switching — this is the safe default, since silently switching on an ambiguous reply risks misattributing credits just as badly as never asking at all. Remove only the pending_switch_to field, leave ticket_id, credits_at_ticket_start, and episode_id exactly as they were, briefly note you're staying on the current ticket, then continue with their original request normally. (C2) Otherwise (no pending_switch_to set), check whether the user's CURRENT message clearly indicates they are now working on or actively planning a SPECIFIC different Jira ticket than the one saved — i.e. it mentions another ticket ID matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ in a context suggesting real work or planning on it (not a passing reference, a comparison to past work, or an example). If so, do NOT proceed with their request yet — ask to confirm: "You're currently tracked on <the saved ticket_id> — are you switching to <the mentioned ticket ID>?", and write pending_switch_to set to that mentioned ticket ID into current-ticket.json, merged in alongside the existing ticket_id/credits_at_ticket_start/episode_id (do not touch those three fields yet), then wait for their next message to be treated as the answer per (C1). If no different ticket is clearly indicated, do nothing extra and proceed with the request normally, exactly as before this whole mid-session-switch logic existed.
